items.summary: A Special Court in Bengaluru has acquitted sitting Congress Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) BK Sangamesha (BK Sangameshwar) and four others in a 2010 case involving allegations of an attack on one C Mahesh Kumar and his sister Jayamma at Shivamogga. An Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Shivaprasad KB acquitted Sangamesha, BK Mohan, Ganesh, Basavaraj and Jagadeesh alias Jagannath. Judge Shivaprasad KB Sangamesha and the four other accused had been charged with the offences of criminal conspiracy under Section 120-B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), rioting under Section 147, attempt to murder under Section 307 read with Section 149 (unlawful assembly), and voluntarily causing grievous hurt under Section 326 read with Section 149 of the IPC. The trial court, however, found glaring defects in the probe. It also observed that at one stage of the investigation, a mentally ill man named Jagadish was made a scapegoat to shield the politically influential accused. In 2018, Jagadish was discharged from the case after the court noted that he was mentally unfit to give evidence. items.title: Husband's girlfriend cannot be booked for cruelty to wife under Section 85 BNS: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a woman paramour who was accused of ruining the married relationship of a couple and intimidating the wife. Justice M Nagaprasanna said that the law is settled that a paramour cannot be accused of the offence of cruelty against wife against Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) since she is not a relative of the husband. In this regard, the Court relied on the Supreme Court's decision in Dechamma IM @ Dechamma Koushik v State of Karnataka in which it was held that a girlfriend of a married man cannot be construed as his relative. "In the light of the bedrock of the law elucidated by the Apex Court, if the facts obtaining in the case at hand are observed, a paramour of the husband - accused No.1 cannot be termed as a relative of the husband," it said. items.title: Supreme Court shifting to ecocentric approach; no automatic precedence for human interests: Justice BV Nagarathna
items.summary: The Supreme Court is pushing for a shift from an anthropocentric to an ecocentric approach in environmental cases, Justice BV Nagarathna recently said. Under ecocentric approach, human interests would not automatically take precedence over those of the non-human world, she explained. “This entails recognising that human interests do not, by virtue of being human, enjoy automatic precedence over the interests of the non-human world; rather, we bear obligations towards non-human life that exist independently of their utility to us,” she said. The judge was speaking at the valedictory session of the National Green Tribunal’s International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”. Justice Nagarathna said environmental adjudication require courts to look beyond completed violations and deal with risks that were unfolding in real time, often amid scientific uncertainty and with potentially irreversible consequences. “In that sense, environmental adjudication is an exercise in foresight, requiring courts to govern the present with an alert consciousness of the future,” she said. items.title: TN Cong leader tells TNM he alerted Chennai cop on Veeramani in November 2024
items.summary: The child sexual assault case involving Gem Granites owner R Veeramani is taking a fresh twist as it emerges that the Chennai police were alerted to the crime as early as November 2024. MP Ranjan Kumar, President of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee’s Scheduled Caste Department, told TNM that when the matter came to his knowledge in 2024, he sought an appointment with the then Additional Commissioner of Police, South, N Kannan and handed over a complaint against Veeramani. The current version of the police is that they only became aware of Veeramani’s alleged crimes in October 2025, when an activist approached them with a pen drive containing visuals of a purported minor girl being sexually assaulted. Ranjan shared with TNM screenshots of his purported chats with Kannan, dated November 20, 2024, in which he asked for an appointment to give a complaint. The screenshot, however, does not make an explicit mention of the case or of Veeramani. After initial messages on 20 November 2024, the next day Ranjan Kumar asked for an appointment. items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Police Special Investigation Team (SIT) on Wednesday, September 23, filed a chargesheet against eight accused in the alleged theft and embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya. The chargesheet, comprising around 74,000 pages along with supporting documents, annexures, exhibits and other evidence, was filed before a local court. The chargesheet was filed roughly 90 days after the case was registered. Kul Shekhar Singh of the Legal Aid Defence Council, who represents the accused, said the chargesheet was filed by the investigating officer under various provisions, including those relating to criminal breach of trust and the Prevention of Corruption Act. The eight accused named in the case are Avinash Shukla, Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra, Manish Kumar Yadav, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav and Subhash Srivastava. They are currently in judicial custody.
